one_line: A shared digital-twin floor plan for designing and connecting smart homes with an agent.
what_it_does: Portego lets a person and browser agent create and edit structured floors, rooms, openings, and devices, then bind the model to real hardware through a local gateway.
leverage_rationale: The shared structured home document and typed operations make agent collaboration materially more reliable than pixel-level canvas driving, while preserving human edits and enabling gateway binding.
leverage_evidence: Description names home.add_room, home.add_device, home.get_document, and home.apply_changes.
Agent and editor write/read the same validated home model.
Frame sheet shows agent prompt, evolving floor-plan UI, and gateway setup stages.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent design-to-gateway flow and frames show the floor plan and gateway stages, though successful real-device control is not fully demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Demo reported alive and public repository exists.
Three frame sheets show populated room/device canvas and gateway configuration.
Description explains outbound WebSocket gateway and shared model.
impact_rationale: Smart-home setup is a real fragmented problem, and a room/device digital twin plus local binding could provide substantial value to homeowners and installers.
impact_evidence: Clearly identified smart-home setup problem.
Workflow covers design, refinement, and physical-device binding.
Local gateway avoids exposed inbound home ports.
creativity_rationale: The combination of conversational floor-plan design, shared human-agent editing, and a physical gateway is a fresh and ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Digital twin is jointly manipulated by person and agent.

red_flags: Frame sheets do not conclusively prove real hardware actuation.

standouts: Shared structured state between agent and human editor.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP leverage, credible smart-home impact, and unusually coherent agent-plus-canvas-plus-hardware concept.

leverage_rationale: Structured listings, negotiation, approval, balances, manifests, and reversible delivery are substantially more dependable through WebMCP than UI scraping, with agents participating in the same transaction state.

leverage_rationale: It addresses the authoring bottleneck directly: instead of requiring code-defined tools, a recorded workflow becomes structured agent capability with human approval and versioning.

standouts: Strong no-code answer to WebMCP tool-definition friction.

one_line: An evidence ledger where agents propose bounded work and named humans decide what becomes canonical history.
what_it_does: Actalume stores project contracts, agent-proposed work bricks, typed evidence receipts, review requests, and immutable human-approved canonical history without giving agents approval authority.
leverage_rationale: Typed, inspectable custody operations and shared evidence state directly address the unreliability of agent summaries; human approval is deliberately outside the agent tool surface.
leverage_evidence: Six named WebMCP tools expose contract, proposal, evidence, review, and history operations.

execution_rationale: The product surfaces agree around a bounded evidence-and-review workflow, and the frame sheet visibly demonstrates the intended chain-of-custody interface; implementation details are claimed rather than independently run here.
execution_evidence: Alive demo and public repository.

impact_rationale: Teams governing agent work have a concrete need to distinguish claims from verified, human-canonical decisions; the system addresses accountability and auditability directly.
impact_evidence: Specific workflow from request through evidence and human review.
Project contracts define allowed/prohibited actions and completion rules.

creativity_rationale: The chain-of-custody framing and explicit separation of agent work from human project truth form a strong, original governance interaction model.

advance_reason: High WebMCP indispensability, coherent demonstrated governance workflow, and strong impact for accountable agent operations.
